The simulation uses OpenFOAM with the solver rhoCentralFoam as specified in system/controlDict.
The working fluid is air modeled as a perfect gas using hePsiThermo with equationOfState set to perfectGas and transport set to sutherland in constant/thermophysicalProperties.
The mesh is 2D (x–y plane) extruded exactly one cell in the z-direction; the frontAndBack boundary patch is set to type empty.
The nozzle inlet has a transverse height of 0.02 m in the y-direction.
The computational domain extends 10 inlet heights above the nozzle, 10 inlet heights below the nozzle, and 20 inlet heights downstream (in the x-direction) to accommodate jet expansion.
The upstream extent of the domain (upstream of the nozzle throat) is 5 inlet heights to allow the flow to establish.
The inlet boundary condition for U is fixedValue with uniform (686 0 0) m/s.
The inlet boundary condition for p is fixedValue with uniform 101325 Pa.
The inlet boundary condition for T is fixedValue with uniform 300 K.
The far-field outlet boundary condition for p is waveTransmissive.
The far-field outlet boundary condition for T is waveTransmissive.
The far-field outlet boundary condition for U is zeroGradient.
All solid wall boundaries (top, bottom, and any nozzle wall surfaces) use noSlip for U.
The frontAndBack patch is type empty for all fields (U, p, T, rho, etc.).
The simulation is transient with a fixed time step; the end time, time step value, and number of steps are to be set by the user in system/controlDict.
The mesh is generated with snappyHexMesh or blockMesh to resolve the nozzle-to-domain expansion; cell sizes should be fine near the nozzle exit and coarser in the far-field.
The inlet Mach number is 2.0, consistent with U = 686 m/s at T = 300 K and p = 101325 Pa for air (gamma = 1.4, R = 287 J/(kg·K)).
